# Dimension of an algebra generated by commuting endomorphisms

`Langlands.CommutingEndomorphismDimensionStatement.{uV}` is a Prop-valued
definition. It states an estimate and supplies no proof.

For every finite-dimensional complex vector space `V`, every natural number
`l`, and every pairwise commuting family `a : Fin l → Module.End ℂ V`, put
`D = Module.finrank ℂ (Algebra.adjoin ℂ (Set.range a))` and
`m = Module.finrank ℂ V`. The proposition is

```text
D ^ (2 ^ l) ≤ m ^ (2 ^ (l + 1) - 2).
```

All powers and the subtraction in this formula are natural-number operations.
The unital generated subalgebra includes scalars; the unit is not counted
as a generator. No nilpotence, cyclic vector, joint diagonalizability or
simplicity hypothesis is imposed. The carrier universe `uV` is arbitrary.

This is a derived reformulation of Bernstein–Zelevinsky (1976), Lemma 4.10,
printed p.39; its proof is in §4.12, printed p.40. The registered source is
`bernstein-zelevinsky-1976-representations-gln`, retained original SHA256
`72dc22eb9991112936a88327f00d0f02a16a2bf8747518ca0ecfeeadd188e50c`.
The source bounds the dimension by `m^(2 - 2^(1-l))`, using real powers.
Here `1-l` is subtraction in the real exponent, not truncated natural
subtraction. Printed pp.39–40 are zero-based PDF pages 38–39.
For `m > 0`, raising that estimate to the positive integer power `2^l`
gives precisely the natural-power inequality above, since
`(2 - 2^(1-l)) * 2^l = 2^(l+1) - 2`. Conversely, monotonicity of that
positive power recovers the real estimate. These equivalences explain
provenance and are not proofs supplied by this module.

The case `l = 0` says `D ≤ 1`, because the algebra generated by the empty
family consists of scalar endomorphisms. The case `m = 0` has `D = 0`:
for `l = 0` the right side is `0^0 = 1`, and for positive `l` both sides
are zero. Thus the statement includes these edge cases without extra
positivity assumptions.

This lemma is the separate linear-algebra input to
`Langlands.SandwichSimpleModuleDimensionBoundStatement`. Burnside and a
sandwich spanning hypothesis yield `m² ≤ q² D`. Raising to `2^l`, using
the present estimate, and cancelling a power of positive `m` yields
`m ≤ q^(2^l)`. The simple-module statement does not assume this lemma as data. Its proof
uses the existing general-field helper
`Langlands.CommutingDimension.commuting_dimension_nat` from
`Langlands.Algebra.CommutingDimensionPrimary`. That helper already proves
the natural-power estimate; the present module independently exposes the
requested complex-vector-space proposition as a named proof target. It
imports no proof and changes no existing Library declaration.
